Here’s how to set up and perform the incline upper chest press. This exercise is going to emphasize the clavicular (upper) portion of your chest.

00:00 Set Up
First adjust the seat so that the end of the handles are right around the crease of your armpit, or just about the middle of your chest. As you can see, if I adjust too high, those handles fall too low, around my nipple area, and if I adjust too low, those handles rise too high, somewhere around my shoulder. In both cases, this will limit my range of motion potentially rolling my shoulders forward, so always make sure to find that sweet spot in the middle. 

Next, grip the handles so that in your starting position, your forearms point directly forward. As you can see, when I grip too far, my forearms point outwards, and when I grip too close, they point inwards. Both can potentially lead to elbow pain, so definitely make sure you are gripping the right spot. Feel free to do a couple practice reps to find this, while of course adjusting the seat as needed. Personally, I always use setting 6, and then place my thumbs right on the end of the handles, so that my grip is roughly the same each time. 

0:45 Concentric
From here, let’s begin the movement. So while keeping your shoulders down, and your posture upright, get into that starting position, and gently lift the weight off the stopper. Then, without wasting too much time, drive your elbows up and in, and think of pushing your biceps together to flex your chest at the top. Now notice how I am keeping my elbows directly in line with that pressing angle. They’re not tilting downwards, and they’re not tilting up, they’re staying exactly in line that entire time. This is going to keep that bias on your upper chest, as you are now matching your arm path, with the direction of those upper chest fibers, for a much more comfortable press. 

Also, don’t intentionally try and squeeze your back or pin your shoulders to the seat, just let your shoulder blades move naturally, as long as you aren’t pushing them excessively forward. 

1:23 Eccentric
Then, while maintaining this technique, explode with as much force as possible, all the way to the end for a full lockout and a brief pause at the top, before controlling the weight down, again keeping those elbows in line, all the way back to the starting position. 

For some people you might not be able to get all the way back due to mobility, but really try your best to go as far as possible without your shoulders rolling forward. And at the bottom, don’t just let go of the weight, maintain that tension, and repeat this process for all of your remaining reps.

1:46 Full Rep
Yes, that means even when the weight gets challenging, do not start rounding your back or excessively puffing out your torso to compensate. Maintain that rigid posture, keep that back against the pad, and let your chest do all the work.
